request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now have an end date (a to-date), and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works now:** for a claim, the rate used is still the one with the latest from-date on or before the claim's date. If that rate has a to-date and the claim is dated after it, the due is **n/a**. An earlier rate does not take over again. For example, with a grade A rate of 10.00 from the start and 20.00 from 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-07, a claim dated 2026-03-08 is n/a.

Everything that uses due follows from this without further changes. The server's lookup in `Rates.on` and the browser's in `rateFor` both apply the new rule, so totals skip the n/a, a statement records n/a, and the late charge has nothing to add to.

**Changes:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V26__rate_to.sql`, adds a nullable `to_date` column to the rate table.
- **Server:**
  - Rates now carry a `to` field. A to-date before the from-date is refused, and so is one that isn't a real date. A refused rate stores nothing and writes no audit record.
  - `RATE_SET` adds `to=<date>` at the end of the line only when a to-date was given, so the existing fields are unchanged.
  - A to-date with no from-date is accepted: the rate runs from the beginning of time through that date.
- **Front end:** the rate form has a new "To" date field (`rate-form-to`), and each rate row shows its to-date (`rate-to`). The form also refuses a to-date before the from-date before sending anything to the server.

Setting a rate again for the same grade and from-date still replaces it, including its to-date.
